newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesia to limit expatriate staff in hotels.
newsitem.headline: Indonesia to limit expatriate staff in hotels.

text.p: Indonesia has said five-star foreign hotel chains must form local subsidiaries and limit the number of expatriates in top management to no more than three by the year 2000, the Jakarta Post newspaper reported on Thursday.

"The requirement to establish joint ventures and the limitation of foreign executives were stipulated in the (Tourism, Post and Telecommunications) Minister's decree issued on November 7," Director-General of Tourism, Andi Mappi Sammeng, was quoted as saying.
The report quoted Andi as saying international hotels could set up joint-ventures with Indonesian partners or wholly owned subsidiaries under the decree, which only affects five-star hotels.
A separate ruling on lower-star hotels would be issued soon, Andi said.
Most international hotel chains operate in Indonesia, including the Hyatt Corp, Forte Plc's Meridien and Hilton Hotels Corp, which all operate five-star hotels.
Some hotels have already set up Indonesian firms such as Hilton International Indonesia, a unit of Hilton Hotels Corp.
